messages:
alex: Heads up — onboarding orca-miniX-int4 hit repeated OOMs on canary when max_new_tokens > 512 and batch_size >= 6. memory fragmentation looks suspicious.

maria: Ugh. saw a couple of those in metrics this morning. p95 latency spikes too?

alex: Yep. p95 + mem spike before OOM: heap freelist drops to near 0, kernel logs show repeated alloc_fail. Example log snippet:

alex: ```
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] ERROR alloc: gpu_alloc failed size=1.2G free=1.1G
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] WARN kv_cache: eviction thr attempt
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] OOM
```

suresh: Do we see this only on int4 variant or also int8/float16?

alex: So far only int4 build (q4_k_mapped). int8 builds stable. Hypothesis: quant layout + prefetch + large max_new_tokens triggers lots of small allocations and fragmentation.

jen: Any pattern on request shape? long context + many short generations or single long generation?

maria: Mostly long context (4k) + generate ~700 tokens. Canary config used default max_new_tokens=768 to match prod target.

suresh: Can we repro locally with microfixture? I'll run a stress harness: batch sizes 2..8, max_new_tokens 128..1024, with and without prefetch.

alex: Thanks. Also tried toggling KV prefetch and saw fragmentation reduce when prefetch=false but latency worsened ~30ms.

infra-bot: CI canary run queued for orca-miniX-int4 with harness id cmr-20260315-1 :ok_hand:

suresh: Quick update — reproed with harness, consistent OOM at batch 6+ and max_new_tokens >= 512. Repro steps I used:

suresh: ```bash
# stress harness
python harness/run_prefetch_stress.py \
  --model orca-miniX-int4 \
  --batch-sizes 2 4 6 8 \
  --max-new 128 256 512 768 1024 \
  --context-len 4096
```

suresh: Memory profiles show many small freelist entries not reusable. evict-priority bumped but allocator churn remains.

maria: Possible mitigations:
- lower default max_new_tokens for int4 to 256
- enable soft microbatching (split large max_new into multiple micro-steps)
- increase freelist bucket sizes or run slot compactor more often
- disable aggressive prefetch for int4 canaries

jen: I prefer changing canary defaults first (safer): set max_new_tokens_default=256 for int4 model family and set rollout guard. Also add auto-fallback to int8 when hosts hit mem frag > threshold.

alex: Agree. For perf-critical workloads we'd lose some convenience but avoid OOMs.

suresh: I'll prototype microbatching patch; cheap to implement: when request.max_new_tokens > 256 and batch_size>1, split into micro batches of 256 and stitch outputs. Might increase total latency but keeps memory bounded.

maria: If microbatching increases tail latency too much, we can gate it by latency SLO: only microbatch when expected gen > 512 and p95 latency budget > X.

jen: Action items:
1) maria: update canary defaults for orca-miniX-int4 -> max_new_tokens 256 + disable prefetch (temp) [ETA: today]
2) suresh: prototype microbatching and run regression harness [ETA: 48h]
3) alex: add a runtime metric for freelist_saturation and a rollout guard that flips to int8 when > 0.8 for >5m [ETA: this week]

alex: I'll post follow-up logs once defaults flipped.

infra-bot: Canary default change deployed for orca-miniX-int4 (PR #4527) — monitoring for 1h :rocket:

maria: quick smoke: after default flip, no OOMs in 1h on canary traffic. p95 latency +12ms when prefetch off.

suresh: microbatch prototype looks promising — no OOMs under the stress harness even at batch 8 and max_new 1024, end-to-end latency up ~18% but tail stable.

jen: Great. Let's keep the default change permanent and consider microbatch as opt-in feature for heavy workloads, with A/B.

alex: Thanks all. I'll open a playbook note summarizing root cause (int4 allocation churn + prefetch + large max_new_tokens) and mitigation steps.

maria: :thumbsup:

suresh: filing follow-up tickets for freelist compactor tuning and allocator metrics.
